_source: Estimator's annotated LV schematic: SB/4 Daltons LV panelboard, 12 outgoing MCCBs.
_why: The SECOND annotated drawing, and it exercises what the first did not. PB1
wrote its frame/trip pair inline ("100/125 A"); this one STACKS the two
figures. PB1 said "GREY BY OTHERS" in words; this one greys items and says
nothing. PB1 drew feeds as boards; this one captions each way with the
sub-board it supplies. And this one lists its cable sizes once at the side,
tied to ways only by which line a way touches.
A target, not a recording. No model has read this drawing in this environment.
test-schematic-fixture.mjs asserts the standing orders instruct an agent to
look for every field used here.

incomer._note: Drawn as a switch symbol labelled 250A. Simpler than PB1's chain — no meter, SPD or CT on the incomer here.

_board_cables_note: Listed ONCE at the side and tied to ways only by which line each way touches. Held at board level deliberately: attaching a size to a way the drawing does not explicitly link would be an invention.

ways._note: Caption reads DB/LM/0/2 POWER in the crop; the LM/P prefix is ambiguous at this resolution.
Setting stacked ABOVE frame: 63A over 100A. One device, not two.
Caption drawn in grey with no wording to explain it — existing, future or by others.

_ways_note: Ways 10-12 carry devices whose captions are outside the crop. Listed rather than dropped: an unread way is what the completeness check exists to surface.

flags.message: Ways 7 and 8 (DB/PL5 DALTONS 4, LIFT) are drawn greyed with no wording. Confirm whether existing, future or by others before pricing.
Cable sizes are listed at board level; the drawing does not label which way takes which.

totals_for_review._note: What deterministic code should compute from the rows above. No agent returns these.
